correctness.rationale: At ab=2/5 the Zibulski–Zeevi matrix has 2 rows and 5 columns. Explicit even/odd Laurent Zak terms for Q2 and neighboring sample values x,x+2/5,x+4/5 yield two exact cubic determinants in t=z². Independently expanded both: left–left h(-t³+2t²+2epsilon t+1) and left–central -h t(t-1)²+(epsilon-u)(A+Bt). Both exclude ±1 unit roots by signs and nonreal unit pairs by cubic coefficient/root-product constraints. Reflection gives right-hand pairs; four position cases for epsilon>1/10 cover x∈[0,1/5], so a continuous compact torus full-row-rank argument implies uniform positive frame bound. For epsilon≤1/10, at x=epsilon,z=-1 all five wrapped samples lie in the central Zak-zero interval so a row vanishes, preventing a frame. Used the quoted rational-density Zibulski–Zeevi equivalence, not finite samples, to conclude iff b>21/10.
residual_risks: Relies on standard matrix normalization, Zak quasi-periodicity and reflected column equivalence; no claims for other b regions or densities.
